sections.heading: Hundreds
sections.html:
Number French
100 cent
101 cent un
110 cent dix
200 deux cents
201 deux cent un (no s)
350 trois cent cinquante
999 neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf

Cent rule: cent takes an s when multiplied and nothing follows: deux cents, cinq cent**s. But deux cent trois (no s), cent alone (cent euros, never ~~un cent~~).

sections.heading: Thousands
sections.html:
Number French
1 000 mille (never ~~un mille~~)
1 001 mille un
2 000 deux mille (mille is invariable: never an s)
2 500 deux mille cinq cents
10 000 dix mille
100 000 cent mille
999 999 neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf

sections.heading: Millions and billions
sections.html:
Number French
1 000 000 un million
2 000 000 deux millions
1 000 000 000 un milliard
3 000 000 000 trois milliards
  • Million and milliard are nouns: they take s in the plural and need de before a noun: un million d'habitants, deux milliards de dollars.
  • But deux millions cinq cent mille personnes (no de if followed by another number).
  • Careful: un billion in French = 10¹² (an English trillion). English "billion" = un milliard.

sections.heading: Hyphens
sections.html: Traditionally, hyphens only link numbers under 100 (vingt-deux). Since the 1990 spelling reform, all numbers can be hyphenated (deux-cent-vingt-et-un). Both are accepted.

sections.heading: Years
sections.html: 1789 = mille sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf (or dix-sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf); 2026 = deux mille vingt-six.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Canada has 41 million inhabitants." / "It costs 3.99 dollars."
exercises.answer: *Le Canada a quarante et un millions d'habitants.* / *Ça coûte trois dollars quatre-vingt-dix-neuf.* (*3,99 $*)
